statement:
The score is the gradient (the vector of partial derivatives) of the natural logarithm of the likelihood function with respect to an m-dimensional parameter vector θ:
$$s(\theta; x) \equiv \frac{\partial \log \mathcal{L}(\theta; x)}{\partial \theta}$$
which yields a $(1 \times m)$ row vector at each value of $\theta$ and $x$, indicating the sensitivity of the likelihood (its derivative normalized by its value).

properties.property: The expected value of the score evaluated at any parameter value θ is zero: $\operatorname{E}(s \mid \theta) = 0$.
properties.why: under regularity conditions allowing interchange of derivative and integral, $\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \int_{\mathcal{X}} f(x; \theta)\,dx = \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} 1 = 0$

properties.property: The variance of the score equals the Fisher information matrix, which is the negative expected value of the Hessian of the log-likelihood: $\operatorname{Var}(s(\theta)) = \operatorname{E}(s(\theta) s(\theta)^{\mathsf{T}}) = -\operatorname{E}\left(\frac{\partial^2 \log \mathcal{L}}{\partial \theta \,\partial \theta^{\mathsf{T}}}\right) = \mathcal{I}(\theta)$.
properties.why: differentiating $\operatorname{E}(s \mid \theta) = 0$ with respect to $\theta^{\mathsf{T}}$ yields the sum of the expected Hessian and the expected outer product of the score

properties.property: The score represents the derivative of the likelihood normalized by its value: $s = \frac{1}{\mathcal{L}} \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \theta}$.
properties.why: direct application of the derivative of the natural logarithm to the likelihood function

properties.property: The likelihood-ratio test statistic is expressed as twice the integral of the score function: $-2[\log \mathcal{L}(\theta_0) - \log \mathcal{L}(\hat{\theta})] = 2\int_{\theta_0}^{\hat{\theta}} s(\theta)\,d\theta$.
properties.why: fundamental theorem of calculus applied to the log-likelihood derivative

assumptions.assumption: Regularity conditions on the density function f(x; θ) permit the interchange of integration over the sample space and differentiation with respect to θ (Leibniz integral rule).
assumptions.breaks_when: The support of the distribution depends on the parameter θ, or f(x; θ) is not differentiable with respect to θ.

assumptions.assumption: The likelihood function L(θ; x) is strictly positive and differentiable with respect to θ.
assumptions.breaks_when: The likelihood is zero (logarithm is undefined) or non-differentiable at θ.

failure_modes.cause: Failure of regularity conditions permitting differentiation under the integral sign over the sample space (e.g., parameter-dependent support boundaries).

failure_modes.signature: Score vector components are undefined, infinite, or division by zero occurs
failure_modes.cause: The likelihood function L(θ; x) reaches zero or is non-differentiable with respect to parameter θ.
